questions.q: The chapter's autonomous statistics engine uses velocity-adjusted staleness thresholds based on sys.dm_db_stats_properties. What are they?
options: 2% modification ratio for tables over 100M rows, 5% for tables over 10M rows, 10% otherwise
A flat 20% of rows plus 500 for all tables, matching the SQL Server default
2% for every table regardless of size
50% for tables under 10M rows, 10% for larger tables
questions.explain: The staleness detection query sets stale_threshold_pct to 2.0 for rows > 100M, 5.0 for rows > 10M, and 10.0 otherwise — tighter than the ~20%+500 reactive default.

questions.q: What fragmentation bands drive the autonomous REORGANIZE vs REBUILD decision?
options: 10–30% → REORGANIZE; above 30% → REBUILD
5–10% → REORGANIZE; above 10% → REBUILD
30–60% → REORGANIZE; above 60% → REBUILD
Any fragmentation above 5% → REBUILD immediately
questions.explain: The chapter's decision query emits REORGANIZE for avg_fragmentation_in_percent BETWEEN 10 AND 30 and REBUILD for fragmentation above 30.

questions.q: Why does the chapter require RESUMABLE = ON on autonomous index rebuilds, and how does the scheduler handle paused operations?
options: It makes rebuilds run faster by using parallel threads; the scheduler kills paused operations
It is required for compatibility with columnstore indexes; paused operations are ignored

A resumable rebuild interrupted by a workload spike or failover pauses instead of losing progress, and the scheduler checks sys.index_resumable_operations each cycle to resume paused operations when the workload gate passes
It allows rebuilds to run online without locks; the scheduler retries them from scratch
questions.explain: RESUMABLE = ON lets an interrupted rebuild pause and resume without losing progress, and the autonomous scheduler polls sys.index_resumable_operations to resume paused operations.

questions.q: The rebuild escalation gate only fires an offline-capable rebuild when all of these hold:
options: Fragmentation > 5%, any time of day, unlimited sessions
Fragmentation > 30% with more than ~1 GB of affected pages, inside the 01:00–05:00 UTC maintenance window, with active user sessions at or below 20
Fragmentation > 60% on a weekend, regardless of active sessions
Page count above 200 pages and fragmentation above 10% during business hours
questions.explain: The escalation engine uses FRAG_PCT_THRESHOLD = 30.0, PAGE_COUNT_MIN = 131072 (~1 GB), a 01:00–05:00 UTC window, and a gate of MAX_ACTIVE_SESSIONS = 20.

questions.q: How does the autonomous index lifecycle engine retire an unused index safely?
options: Drops it immediately when sys.dm_db_index_usage_stats shows zero seeks for 7 days
Keeps it forever — autonomous systems never drop indexes

Tracks created indexes in dba_autonomous_indexes; after a 30-day usage review shows no seeks/scans it marks the index DEFERRED_DROP, disables it for a 14-day observation window to check for plan regressions, then executes the drop
Rebuilds the index with DROP_EXISTING and leaves it disabled
questions.explain: Retirement is staged: 30-day usage review via sys.dm_db_index_usage_stats, DEFERRED_DROP marking, 14-day disabled observation window with plan-regression checks, then the drop.
